newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan port strike could slow cocoa shipments.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan port strike could slow cocoa shipments.

text.p: A dockers strike at Abidjan port entered its third day on Wednesday and shipping sources said it could slow cocoa exports at a critical shipping period.

They said the strike was taking place at the end of the month when many exporters ship their cocoa after holding out to see prices. There were no details of the exact impact of the strike on Christmas Day.
A duty officer at Abidjan Ports Authority told Reuters talks were continuing between management and union leaders, but there was as yet no sign of an end to the pay strike.
"They are still talking and the port strike continues. There is no loading or discharging. Nothing is happening," he said.
Strike leaders said the action started on Monday and would continue until a pay dispute was resolved.
The port of San Pedro to the west, which like Abidjan handles Ivory Coast's cocoa exports, was not affected.
"We have no fixed salaries, we are paid by the hour and we have been working in this condition for years," declared Zadi Nadje Daniel, a spokesman for the dockers.
"What we want now is fixed salaries plus annual bonuses as exists in other sectors," told reporters on Tuesday, adding, "We are not going back to work until our demands are met."
No comment was available from management.
